paper_title: First results of the CAST-RADES haloscope search for axions at 34.67 $μ$eV
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, canonical axion-photon coupling constant
notes: First results from CAST-RADES haloscope searching for axion dark matter at 34.67 μeV. Exclusion limit g_aγ ≳ 4×10^-13 GeV^-1 set over narrow mass range 34.6738 μeV < m_a < 34.6771 μeV with 95% credibility level. This is a measured exclusion limit from physics data taken in 2018 inside the CAST dipole magnet. The limit represents a significant improvement (>2 orders of magnitude) over previous CAST solar axion search results at this mass. Local dark matter density ρ_DM = 0.45 GeV/cm^3 used in sensitivity calculation per equation (1.1). The mass range is very narrow (Δm ≈ 0.33 neV), so encoded as a horizontal line at the coupling limit. No axion signal detected above noise (maximum local significance 3.67σ, global significance 1.71σ after look-elsewhere correction). | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.92, 51)) | Vision: Figure 9 shows the axion-photon coupling versus axion mass phase-space. The inset zooms into the CAST-RADES measurement range (34.6738 μeV < m_a < 34.6771 μeV), showing the detailed structure of the limit. The green band represents measurement uncertainty (~10% error). The boundary was traced from the zoomed inset region and extrapolated smoothly across the full mass range shown. KSVZ and DFSZ theoretical model lines are shown for reference (orange bands).
